Class ActionHandler

java.lang.Object
dev.tamboui.tui.bindings.ActionHandler
public final class ActionHandler extends Object
Dispatches events to registered action handlers.

ActionHandler wraps a Bindings instance and allows registering callbacks for specific actions. When an event is dispatched, it is matched against the bindings and the corresponding handlers are invoked. 

ActionHandler handler = new ActionHandler(BindingSets.vim())
    .on(Actions.QUIT, e -> runner.quit())
    .on("save", this::save)
    .on("delete", this::delete);

// In event handler:
if (handler.dispatch(event)) {
    return EventResult.HANDLED;
}

    • on

      public ActionHandler on(String action, Consumer<Event> handler)
      Registers a handler for the specified action.

      Multiple handlers can be registered for the same action; they will be invoked in registration order when the action is triggered.

      Parameters:
      action - the action name to handle
      handler - the handler to invoke when the action is triggered
      Returns:
      this handler for method chaining

    • on

      public ActionHandler on(String action, BiConsumer<Event,String> handler)
      Registers a handler for the specified action that also receives the action name.

      This is useful when the same handler is registered for multiple actions and needs to know which action triggered it.

      Multiple handlers can be registered for the same action; they will be invoked in registration order when the action is triggered.

      Parameters:
      action - the action name to handle
      handler - the handler to invoke, receiving the event and action name
      Returns:
      this handler for method chaining

    • fire

      public boolean fire(String action, Event event)
      Fires a named action directly, bypassing bindings resolution.

      Unlike dispatch(Event), this method does not resolve the action from the event via bindings. Instead, the action name is provided explicitly, allowing programmatic triggering of actions.

      This is useful when an element interaction (e.g., a click) should trigger a named action that is also bound to a keyboard shortcut: 

      // Key binding: Ctrl+S triggers "save" (via bindings)
// Element click also fires "save" (via fire):
text("Save").focusable().on(MouseTrigger.click(), e -> handler.fire("save", e));
      Parameters:
      action - the action name to fire
      event - the event that triggered this action
      Returns:
      true if the action was handled (handlers registered and invoked), false otherwise

    • fire

      public boolean fire(String action)
      Fires a named action without an originating event.

      An ActionEvent is created to represent the programmatic trigger. This is useful when no input event is involved (e.g., firing an action from a timer or application logic).

      Parameters:
      action - the action name to fire
      Returns:
      true if the action was handled (handlers registered and invoked), false otherwise

    • dispatch

      public boolean dispatch(Event event)
      Dispatches an event to registered handlers.

      The event is matched against the bindings. If a matching action is found and handlers are registered for that action, all handlers are invoked in registration order.

      Parameters:
      event - the event to dispatch
      Returns:
      true if the event was handled (action found with registered handlers), false otherwise

    • registerAnnotated

      public <T> ActionHandler registerAnnotated(T target)
      Discovers and registers action handlers from the target object.

      First attempts to find generated ActionHandlerRegistrar implementations via ServiceLoader. If no registrar is found for the target's exact class, falls back to reflection-based discovery of @OnAction annotated methods.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the target type
      Parameters:
      target - the object containing @OnAction annotated methods
      Returns:
      this handler for method chaining
